subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots inherit OpenClaw host overrides such as path-to-regexp, or should OpenClaw scope those overrides away from plugin-owned dependency graphs and add targeted validation or Doctor recovery?
rationale: Both directions change a compatibility and supply-chain boundary: host overrides protect OpenClaw's reviewed dependency graph, but applying them to third-party plugin roots can break valid plugin-owned dependency ranges.

options.title: Scope Managed-Root Overrides
options.body: Change managed npm roots so OpenClaw host overrides do not override plugin-owned dependencies unless explicitly safe, and add regression coverage for Express 4 and Express 5 graphs.

options.title: Add Validator Only
options.body: Keep current override propagation but detect Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts during install or Doctor and fail with a clear recovery message.

options.title: Keep Plugin-Owned Workaround
options.body: Document that Express 4 plugins must ship their own override or migrate to Express 5, accepting that users can still hit runtime-only failures.

recommendation.title: Scope Managed-Root Overrides
recommendation.body: Change managed npm roots so OpenClaw host overrides do not override plugin-owned dependencies unless explicitly safe, and add regression coverage for Express 4 and Express 5 graphs.

likelyOwner.reason: The current managed npm override propagation and workspace override lines route most directly through this recent area history.
